title: Operational user configures area-wise offer presentation duration within the allowed range
folder: Backend Services > Matching & Dispatching > Offer Presentation Duration
steps: Scenario: Operational user configures area-wise offer presentation duration within the allowed range Given the operational user is logged into Jeeny Cockpit And the operational user navigates to Configs > Matching & Dispatching And the operational user selects a city When the operational user sets the offer presentation duration to a value between 8 and 20 seconds And the operational user saves the configuration Then the configuration should be saved successfully And drivers in the selected city should see ride offers presented for the configured duration And drivers in other cities should be unaffected by this configuration When the operational user attempts to set the offer presentation duration outside the 8–20 second range Then the configuration should not be saved And a validation message should indicate the allowed range is 8 to 20 seconds

title: Feature: Deep Link Redirect to Discounted Price Check Screen
folder: Backend Services > Matching & Dispatching > RCRC DARB Integration
steps: Scenario: User opens a promotional deep link and requests a fully discounted ride Given the user has received a deep link offering a 100% ride discount And the user has the Jeeny app installed And the user is authenticated And the user does not have an active ride in progress When the user clicks the deep link Then the app should open And the user should be taken to the price check screen And the pickup location should be prefilled from the deep link And the destination location should be prefilled from the deep link And the service type should be preselected And the displayed ride price should be 0 And the screen should indicate that a 100% discount has been applied When the user requests the ride Then the ride request should be submitted successfully

title: Verify that a valid access token is successfully generated when sending valid client_id and client_secret credentials
folder: Backend Services > Matching & Dispatching > RCRC DARB Integration > Authentication Token API
preconditions: Valid client_id and client_secret exist in database
steps: Send POST request to /v1/cod_token Include valid client_id and client_secret Include grant_type=client_credentials Verify response
expected: Status: 200 OK Response contains: access_token (JWT format), token_type = "Bearer", expires_in = 2592000 (or configured value), message = "Access token generated successfully." Token is saved in database with metadata Token contains JWT claims: partner_id, token_id, expiration, scopes

title: Scenario: Driver attempts to go online while in an out-of-operating area
folder: Backend Services > Matching & Dispatching > Out-of-Operating Area (OOA/NOA)
steps: Given the driver is in an area where Jeeny does not operate And the driver is currently offline When the driver taps the "Go Online" button Then the "Go Online" button remains disabled And an in-app banner is displayed notifying the driver they are out of the operating area And a push notification is sent with the configured out-of-operating-area title and description And the driver remains offline And the banner and notification content match the customization configured for the driver's city

title: Scenario: Driver moves from online into an out-of-operating area
folder: Backend Services > Matching & Dispatching > Out-of-Operating Area (OOA/NOA)
steps: Given the driver is online and inside an operating area When the driver moves into an area where Jeeny does not operate Then the driver is automatically marked offline And an in-app banner is displayed notifying the driver they are out of the operating area And a push notification is sent with the configured out-of-operating-area title and description And the "Go Online" button becomes disabled And the banner and notification content match the customization configured for the driver's city

title: Scenario: Driver moves back into the operating area from an out-of-operating area
folder: Backend Services > Matching & Dispatching > Out-of-Operating Area (OOA/NOA)
steps: Given the driver is offline because they are in an out-of-operating area When the driver moves back into an area where Jeeny operates Then the driver's status automatically changes to online And a welcome-back in-app banner is displayed for the configured duration And a push notification is sent with the configured welcome-back title and description And the "Go Online" button becomes enabled And the banner and notification content match the customization configured for the driver's city

title: Scenario: Driver attempts to go online while in a non-operating area
folder: Backend Services > Matching & Dispatching > Out-of-Operating Area (OOA/NOA)
steps: Given the driver is in a city where Jeeny operates And the driver's assigned service is not active in their current area And the driver is currently offline When the driver taps the "Go Online" button Then the "Go Online" button remains disabled And an in-app banner is displayed notifying the driver their service is not available in this area And a push notification is sent with the configured non-operating-area title and description And the driver remains offline And the banner and notification content match the customization configured for the driver's city

title: Scenario: Driver moves from online into a non-operating area
folder: Backend Services > Matching & Dispatching > Out-of-Operating Area (OOA/NOA)
preconditions: Background: Given the driver app is installed on the latest supported build And the OOA/NOA feature is enabled for the driver's current city
steps: Given the driver is online and their assigned service is active in their current area When the driver moves into an area where their assigned service is not active Then the driver is automatically marked offline And an in-app banner is displayed notifying the driver their service is not available in this area And a push notification is sent with the configured non-operating-area title and description And the "Go Online" button becomes disabled And the banner and notification content match the customization configured for the driver's city

title: Scenario: Driver moves back into an area where their service is active
folder: Backend Services > Matching & Dispatching > Out-of-Operating Area (OOA/NOA)
preconditions: Background: Given the driver app is installed on the latest supported build And the OOA/NOA feature is enabled for the driver's current city
steps: Given the driver is offline because their assigned service is not active in their current area When the driver moves into an area where their assigned service is active Then the driver's status automatically changes to online And a welcome-back in-app banner is displayed for the configured duration And a push notification is sent with the configured welcome-back title and description And the "Go Online" button becomes enabled And the banner and notification content match the customization configured for the driver's city
